The platform is designed to receive every module of the Salesforce org; Subscription Management is its first domain. ## 1. Introduction and goals | | | |---|---| | Source | Salesforce org, 505 objects described | | Platform scope | Every module of the org, domain by domain: Core customer, Sales, Service, Subscriptions, Activities | | First domain | Subscription, Subscription Line (pilot) | | Reference objects | Account, Contact, Opportunity, Product | | Target | Microsoft Azure: Container Apps, Azure Database for PostgreSQL, Service Bus, Event Hubs, API Management, Front Door, Entra ID, Key Vault, Azure Monitor | | Data in the first domain | Account 22 · Contact 20 · Opportunity 31 · Product 17 · Subscription 107 · Subscription Line 219 | Quality goals, in priority order: **behavioural parity** with Salesforce, **security** at least equal to the org’s, **modularity** so any module can be added or moved on its own, **availability** through a zone failure, **operability** with everything as code. ## 2. Constraints - Each object has exactly one master at any time: Salesforce until its domain cuts over, Azure after. - After the last wave the platform has no dependency on Salesforce. - Salesforce record IDs are kept, so integrations, links and reports keep working. - Platform services only (no virtual machines), in the client’s own tenant and subscription; data stays in the chosen region. - Open standards throughout (PostgreSQL, containers, OpenAPI, CloudEvents, OpenID Connect), so the platform is portable. ## 3. for each owner"] C -- "no" --> E(["Done"]) D --> E classDef job fill:#EAFBF5,stroke:#2CDCAA,color:#1F1F2E; class A,B,D job; ``` ### 6.6 Case routing and escalation Assignment rules route each new case; escalation rules raise cases that miss their target time. Deployment view ### 7.1 Target deployment on Azure One region with three availability zones, a paired region for backups, and private networking in a spoke virtual network connected to the client’s landing zone. Domains release together while they share one deployable. ### 7.4 Availability and recovery | Event | What happens | Target | |---|---|---| | Replica failure | Container Apps replaces the replica; others keep serving | no downtime | | Zone failure | Replicas in other zones serve; the database fails over to its standby zone | about 2 minutes, no data loss | | Region failure | Restore from geo-redundant backup in the paired region | RTO hours, RPO under 1 hour | | Bad release | Move traffic back to the previous revision | minutes | ## 8. Cross-cutting concepts ### 8.1 Data model of the first domain ```mermaid erDiagram Account { varchar id PK varchar name text type varchar billing_country text customer_priority text sla text active numeric numberof_locations text upsell_opportunity varchar sla_serial_number } Contact { varchar id PK varchar name text level varchar languages } Opportunity { varchar id PK varchar name text stage_name numeric amount text delivery_installation_status varchar tracking_number varchar order_number varchar current_generators varchar main_competitors text loss_reason } Product { varchar id PK varchar name } Subscription { varchar id PK varchar subscription_number varchar account_id FK boolean auto_renew varchar cancellation_reason date end_date numeric health_score numeric monthly_recurring_revenue date start_date text status } SubscriptionLine { varchar id PK varchar line_number varchar subscription_id FK numeric quantity numeric unit_price varchar account_name numeric line_total } Account |o--o{ Contact : "Account ID" Account |o--o{ Opportunity : "Account ID" Contact |o--o{ Opportunity : "Contact ID" Subscription ||--|{ SubscriptionLine : "Subscription" Product |o--o{ SubscriptionLine : "Product" Account ||--|{ Subscription : "Account" Contact |o--o{ Subscription : "Primary Contact" Opportunity |o--o{ Subscription : "Source Opportunity" ``` ### 8.2 Security across domains Identity, roles and sharing are one shared model. Every domain schema enforces it with row-level security that calls the same access functions, so a user sees the same records in every module and through every client of the data. ```mermaid flowchart LR STAFF(["Staff"]) --> ENTRA["Entra ID
app roles, groups, MFA"] PORTAL(["Portal users"]) --> EXTID["Entra External ID"] ENTRA --> APP["Domain services
set role and user per request"] EXTID --> APP APP --> RLS["Row-level security policies
in every domain schema"] RLS --> ACC[("Access schema
role hierarchy, groups, teams, territories, share tables")] APP --> COL["Column grants
field-level security"] SFSEC["Salesforce profiles, permission sets, roles, sharing rules"] -. "migrated once, then managed here" .-> ACC ``` | Salesforce concept | Target | |---|---| | Users, single sign-on | Entra ID (staff), Entra External ID (customer and partner portals) | | Profiles and permission sets | Entra app roles and database roles | | Field-level security | Column grants per role | | Org-wide defaults, role hierarchy, sharing rules, teams, territories | Access schema (groups, hierarchy closure, share tables) used by row-level security | | Shield Platform Encryption | Encryption at rest with customer-managed keys in Key Vault | | Field Audit Trail, setup audit | Audit tables and Log Analytics, kept as long as policy requires | | Personal data in sandboxes | Microsoft Purview classification; masked copies in test | #### Roles in the first domain Each profile or permission set becomes a database role; field-level security becomes column grants; subscriptions inherit access from their account. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph SFS["Salesforce"] profile_Admin["Profile: Admin"] profile_Analytics_Cloud_Integration_User["Profile: Analytics Cloud Integration User"] permissionSet_Subscription_Management["Permission set: Subscription_Management"] OWD["Account sharing
(org-wide default)"] end subgraph PG["PostgreSQL"] PG_profile_Admin["role admin"] PG_profile_Analytics_Cloud_Integration_User["role analytics cloud integration user"] PG_permissionSet_Subscription_Management["role subscription_management"] RLS["row-level security
can_access_account()"] COL["column grants
(field-level security)"] end profile_Admin --> PG_profile_Admin PG_profile_Admin --> COL profile_Analytics_Cloud_Integration_User --> PG_profile_Analytics_Cloud_Integration_User PG_profile_Analytics_Cloud_Integration_User --> COL permissionSet_Subscription_Management --> PG_permissionSet_Subscription_Management PG_permissionSet_Subscription_Management --> COL OWD --> RLS SUB["Subscription and lines
inherit access from the account"] --> RLS ``` ### 8.3 Migration waves and system of record Domains move one at a time. Core customer data and every in-use domain start as read copies fed by the change feed; a domain becomes master in Azure in its wave; the core moves last, when nothing left in Salesforce writes to it. | Wave | What happens | |---|---| | Wave 0: foundation | Landing zone, platform services, identity; Core customer and every in-use domain as read copies fed by the Salesforce change feed | | Wave 1: Subscriptions (pilot) | Subscriptions becomes master in Azure; its users and integrations switch; Salesforce keeps a read-only copy | | Wave 2: Sales | Sales becomes master in Azure; its users and integrations switch; Salesforce keeps a read-only copy | | Wave 3: Service | Service becomes master in Azure; its users and integrations switch; Salesforce keeps a read-only copy | | Wave 4: core and activities | Core customer and activities become master in Azure; Salesforce is read-only | | Wave 5: decommission | Final archive taken; licences reduced at renewal | | Domain | Wave 1 | Wave 2 | Wave 3 | Wave 4 | |---|---|---|---|---| | Core customer | Salesforce | Salesforce | Salesforce | Azure | | Sales | Salesforce | Azure | Azure | Azure | | Service | Salesforce | Salesforce | Azure | Azure | | Subscriptions | Azure | Azure | Azure | Azure | | Activities | Salesforce | Salesforce | Salesforce | Azure | #### Load order in the first domain Records load parent first, in dependency order, keeping every Salesforce record ID. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph L0["Level 1"] Account["Account
22 rows"] Product2["Product
17 rows"] end subgraph L1["Level 2"] Contact["Contact
20 rows"] end subgraph L2["Level 3"] Opportunity["Opportunity
31 rows"] end subgraph L3["Level 4"] Subscription__c["Subscription
107 rows"] end subgraph L4["Level 5"] Subscription_Line__c["Subscription Line
219 rows"] end L0 --> L1 L1 --> L2 L2 --> L3 L3 --> L4 ``` ### 8.4 Integration and events | Concern | Standard | |---|---| | External APIs | REST with OpenAPI 3, versioned, through API Management; a Salesforce-compatible facade so callers keep working during the move | | Events between domains | CloudEvents on Service Bus, written through a transactional outbox; consumers are idempotent | | Salesforce change feed | Pub/Sub API (Change Data Capture) into Event Hubs, applied in order per record | | Reads across domains | Published read views only; no domain writes into another domain’s schema | ### 8.5 Adding the next module 1. Discover and design it as a domain; place it on the domain map and the system-of-record matrix. 2. Generate its schema, rules, access policies and API from the same template; publish its read views and events. 3. Start it as a read copy fed by the change feed; run the parity and security tests. 4. Switch its users and integrations in its wave; Salesforce keeps a read-only copy until decommission. ### 8.6 Salesforce products outside the core org | Product | Kind | Route | |---|---|---| | Marketing Cloud Engagement | separate platform | replace with a marketing product, or retain and integrate through the gateway | | Commerce Cloud (B2C) | separate platform | retain and integrate, or replace with a commerce platform | | Data Cloud, Tableau | separate platforms | replace with Microsoft Fabric and Power BI on the new database | | MuleSoft | integration platform | its flows move to API Management, Service Bus and Logic Apps | | Managed packages (for example CPQ) | on the core org | settings and data taken; behaviour rebuilt, replaced or retained per package | ### 8.7 Observability Services and jobs send traces, metrics and logs to Application Insights; Azure resources send diagnostics to Log Analytics; Microsoft Sentinel watches security events. Alerts cover availability, error rate, response time, event backlog, sync lag, database CPU and storage, and failed sign-ins. ### 8.8 Traceability The LLD’s traceability matrix links each Salesforce element to its target design, database object and test. ## 9. Architecture decisions | ADR | Decision | |---|---| | [ADR-002](adr/ADR-002-keep-salesforce-ids.md) | Keep the 18-character Salesforce ID as the primary key | | [ADR-003](adr/ADR-003-generated-columns.md) | Row-local formulas become stored generated columns | | [ADR-004](adr/ADR-004-cross-object-views.md) | Cross-object formulas become views | | [ADR-005](adr/ADR-005-compute-on-read.md) | Date-dependent formulas are computed when read | | [ADR-006](adr/ADR-006-trigger-maintained-rollups.md) | Roll-up summaries are trigger-maintained columns with a recompute job | | [ADR-007](adr/ADR-007-check-constraints.md) | Row-local validation rules become CHECK constraints | | [ADR-008](adr/ADR-008-guard-triggers.md) | Rules needing the previous row or a parent record become BEFORE-trigger guards | | [ADR-009](adr/ADR-009-roles-and-rls.md) | Profiles and permission sets become roles; Salesforce and Azure coexist through the change feed | | [ADR-019](adr/ADR-019-central-access-model.md) | One access model for every domain, enforced by row-level security | | [ADR-020](adr/ADR-020-open-standards.md) | Build on open standards so the platform is portable | ## 10. Quality requirements | Quality | Scenario | How it is measured | |---|---|---| | Parity | Every calculated value and rule outcome matches Salesforce | Automated parity tests, blocking in the release pipeline | | Security | A user sees and edits only what Salesforce allows, in every domain | Security tests per role and domain; row-level security and column grants | | Modularity | A new module is added without changing existing domains | Contract tests on read views and events; schema permissions between domains | | Availability | The service keeps running through the loss of a zone | Zone-redundant services and database; failover drill each quarter | | Performance | Screens respond in under 2 seconds at peak load; sync lag under 1 minute | Application Insights and event-backlog alerts; load test before each wave | | Operability | Any environment can be rebuilt from source | Bicep templates and the pipeline; no manual changes | ## 11. adrs.ADR-001:
# ADR-001: A vendor-neutral blueprint is the contract between extraction and generation

Status: Accepted · Owner: Modelling agent · Blueprint `fc71a1458dce`

## Context

Extractors speak Salesforce; generators speak PostgreSQL. Coupling them directly makes every new source or target a rewrite.

## Decision

All generators read only the blueprint (JSON, validated against blueprint.schema.json, content-hashed). Extraction never talks to generation.

## Consequences

Re-runs are deterministic and diffable; a new target needs one emitter. The schema must evolve with care (versioned).

## Applies to (1)

- `adlc/2-design/modelling/blueprint/blueprint.json`
adrs.ADR-002:
# ADR-002: Keep the 18-character Salesforce ID as the primary key

Status: Accepted · Owner: Modelling agent · Blueprint `fc71a1458dce`

## Context

Integrations, reports and users hold Salesforce IDs; a migration that renumbers records breaks them.

## Decision

Every table keeps the Salesforce ID as its key; new records get IDs in the same format from the runtime.

## Consequences

Links, bookmarks and the compatibility API keep working; keys are text, not integers.

## Applies to (6)

- `Account.Id`
- `Contact.Id`
- `Opportunity.Id`
- `Product2.Id`
- `Subscription__c.Id`
- `Subscription_Line__c.Id`
adrs.ADR-003:
# ADR-003: Row-local formulas become stored generated columns

Status: Accepted · Owner: Modelling agent · Blueprint `fc71a1458dce`

## Context

Formulas that read only their own row are pure functions of the row.

## Decision

Compile them to GENERATED ALWAYS AS … STORED, with blank-as-zero made explicit.

## Consequences

Always correct, indexable, no application code; formulas using TODAY() cannot use this (see ADR-005).

## Applies to (2)

- `Subscription_Line__c.Line_Total__c`
- `Subscription__c.Annual_Value__c`
adrs.ADR-004:
# ADR-004: Cross-object formulas become views

Status: Accepted · Owner: Modelling agent · Blueprint `fc71a1458dce`

## Context

Generated columns cannot read another table.

## Decision

Expose them through a view that joins the parent records.

## Consequences

Always current; reads go through the view.

## Applies to (1)

- `Subscription_Line__c.Account_Name__c`
adrs.ADR-005:
# ADR-005: Date-dependent formulas are computed when read

Status: Accepted · Owner: Modelling agent · Blueprint `fc71a1458dce`

## Context

A stored value using TODAY() would be wrong tomorrow.

## Decision

Compute in the view using app.today(), evaluated in the org’s time zone.

## Consequences

Matches Salesforce, which also evaluates on read.

## Applies to (1)

- `Subscription__c.Days_To_Renewal__c`
adrs.ADR-006:
# ADR-006: Roll-up summaries are trigger-maintained columns with a recompute job

Status: Accepted · Owner: Modelling agent · Blueprint `fc71a1458dce`

## Context

Roll-ups must be filterable and fast, and correct after bulk loads.

## Decision

Statement-level triggers keep totals current; a recompute function rebuilds them after loads and as a safety net.

## Consequences

Fast reads; load mode defers triggers and recomputes once.

## Applies to (2)

- `Subscription__c.Line_Count__c`
- `Subscription__c.Total_Line_Value__c`
adrs.ADR-007:
# ADR-007: Row-local validation rules become CHECK constraints

Status: Accepted · Owner: Modelling agent · Blueprint `fc71a1458dce`

## Context

Rules that read only the row being saved can be enforced by the database itself.

## Decision

Compile to CHECK constraints named after the rule, keeping the Salesforce error message in the mapping.

## Consequences

Enforced for every writer, including integrations and loads.

## Applies to (6)

- `Opportunity.Closed_Won_Requires_Amount`
- `Opportunity.Loss_Reason_Required_When_Lost`
- `Subscription_Line__c.Quantity_Must_Be_Positive`
- `Subscription__c.Active_Requires_MRR`
- `Subscription__c.Cancellation_Reason_Required`
- `Subscription__c.End_Date_After_Start_Date`
adrs.ADR-008:
# ADR-008: Rules needing the previous row or a parent record become BEFORE-trigger guards

Status: Accepted · Owner: Modelling agent · Blueprint `fc71a1458dce`

## Context

PRIORVALUE, ISCHANGED and cross-object rules cannot be CHECK constraints.

## Decision

Generate BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE triggers that raise the Salesforce message.

## Consequences

Same behaviour as Salesforce; order of guards follows Salesforce’s order of execution.

## Applies to (2)

- `Subscription_Line__c.Parent_Not_Cancelled`
- `Subscription__c.No_Reactivation_After_Cancel`
adrs.ADR-009:
# ADR-009: Profiles and permission sets become roles; sharing becomes row-level security

Status: Accepted · Owner: Modelling agent · Blueprint `fc71a1458dce`

## Context

Access must be enforced where the data lives, not only in the app.

## Decision

One database role per profile or permission set, column grants for field-level security, RLS policies for sharing; the app sets the role per request.

## Consequences

Any client of the database gets the same access rules; policies are tested by parity cases.

## Applies to (3)

- `profile:Admin`
- `profile:Analytics Cloud Integration User`
- `permissionSet:Subscription_Management`
adrs.ADR-010:
# ADR-010: Apex is translated by an AI agent and merged only after review

Status: Accepted · Owner: Modelling agent · Blueprint `fc71a1458dce`

## Context

Apex can do anything; deterministic templates cannot cover it.

## Decision

The Logic agent drafts a translation with tests; it is marked reviewed:false until a person approves it at the gate.

## Consequences

Speed of generation with human accountability; nothing generated merges unchecked.

## Applies to (2)

- `apex-trigger:OpportunityTrigger`
- `apex-trigger:SubscriptionTrigger`
adrs.ADR-011:
# ADR-011: Behaviour is accepted only when it matches Salesforce’s own values

Status: Accepted · Owner: Modelling agent · Blueprint `fc71a1458dce`

## Context

Reviewing generated code line by line does not scale.

## Decision

The Verification agent recomputes every calculated value against what Salesforce stored and replays rule cases; CI blocks release on any mismatch.

## Consequences

Correctness is measured, not asserted; new behaviours need new cases.

## Applies to (1)

- `adlc/5-validate/verification/cases.json`
adrs.ADR-012:
# ADR-012: Host on Azure Container Apps and Azure Database for PostgreSQL

Status: Accepted · Owner: Modelling agent · Blueprint `fc71a1458dce`

## Context

The platform will grow to many domains, with web traffic, scheduled jobs and event handlers; the client wants no servers to run and zone-level resilience.

## Decision

Run domain services, jobs and the Salesforce sync on a zone-redundant Azure Container Apps environment, and data on PostgreSQL Flexible Server with zone-redundant high availability.

## Consequences

One hosting model for every domain, with scale-to-demand and event-driven jobs; containers keep the option to move to Kubernetes or another cloud.

## Applies to (2)

- `Azure Container Apps`
- `Azure Database for PostgreSQL`
adrs.ADR-013:
# ADR-013: Staff sign in with Entra ID, portal users with Entra External ID; services use managed identities

Status: Accepted · Owner: Modelling agent · Blueprint `fc71a1458dce`

## Context

Salesforce passwords cannot be exported, and stored service credentials are a leading cause of breaches.

## Decision

OpenID Connect sign-in through Entra ID for staff (matched by Federation ID) and Entra External ID for customer and partner portal users; services reach Key Vault, the database and the event bus with managed identities; integrations use OAuth 2.0 through API Management.

## Consequences

No passwords to migrate or rotate; conditional access and MFA come from the client tenant.

## Applies to (4)

- `Microsoft Entra ID`
- `Entra External ID`
- `Key Vault`
- `API Management`
adrs.ADR-014:
# ADR-014: Data services are reachable only on private endpoints; the edge is Front Door with WAF

Status: Accepted · Owner: Modelling agent · Blueprint `fc71a1458dce`

## Context

Customer and revenue data must not be reachable from the internet.

## Decision

PostgreSQL and Key Vault have private endpoints in a spoke virtual network; the app uses VNet integration; public traffic enters only through Front Door with the Web Application Firewall.

## Consequences

One controlled entry point; deployments and administration go through the pipeline or a bastion.

## Applies to (3)

- `Front Door`
- `Virtual network`
- `Private endpoints`
adrs.ADR-015:
# ADR-015: The platform is split into business domains around a shared core customer domain

Status: Accepted · Owner: Modelling agent · Blueprint `fc71a1458dce`

## Context

Every Salesforce cloud hangs off the same accounts, contacts, users and products, and the org moves module by module.

## Decision

Group objects into domains (core customer, sales, service, subscriptions, activities and later modules), each owning its objects. Any domain may reference the core; other domains are reached only through their published read views and events.

## Consequences

Modules move and change independently; new Salesforce clouds become new domains without touching existing ones.

## Applies to (5)

- `Core customer`
- `Sales`
- `Service`
- `Subscriptions`
- `Activities`
adrs.ADR-016:
# ADR-016: Start as a modular monolith: one deployable and one database, one schema per domain

Status: Accepted · Owner: Modelling agent · Blueprint `fc71a1458dce`

## Context

Salesforce saves related records in one transaction; splitting every domain into its own service and database from day one would lose that and add operational cost.

## Decision

Deploy all domains as modules of one service on one PostgreSQL server, one schema per domain; enforce boundaries with schema permissions and contract tests. Split a domain into its own service or server only when its scale or release cadence requires it.

## Consequences

Integrity inside a domain stays transactional; boundaries are real, so a later split needs no redesign.

## Applies to (2)

- `Domain services`
- `PostgreSQL`
adrs.ADR-017:
# ADR-017: Domains talk through events written with a transactional outbox

Status: Accepted · Owner: Modelling agent · Blueprint `fc71a1458dce`

## Context

A change in one domain often triggers work in another, for example a won opportunity creating a subscription.

## Decision

A domain writes its change and an outbox row in one transaction; a relay publishes it to Service Bus as a CloudEvent; consumers are idempotent. Cases where Salesforce did both in one save are listed and covered by parity tests.

## Consequences

No lost or duplicate side effects; cross-domain effects are eventually consistent within seconds.

## Applies to (2)

- `Service Bus`
- `outbox tables`
adrs.ADR-018:
# ADR-018: Each object has exactly one master at any time; Salesforce and Azure coexist through the change feed

Status: Accepted · Owner: Modelling agent · Blueprint `fc71a1458dce`

## Context

Domains move over months while the rest of the org stays on Salesforce; two systems writing the same record would diverge.

## Decision

A system-of-record matrix names the master of every object per wave. Salesforce changes stream through the Pub/Sub API into Event Hubs and update read copies; Azure writes back only fields that remaining Salesforce features still read. The gateway routes each API call to the current master.

## Consequences

No conflicting writes; each wave is reversible; integrations follow the master without code changes.

## Applies to (3)

- `Event Hubs`
- `Salesforce sync`
- `API Management`
adrs.ADR-019:
# ADR-019: One access model for every domain, enforced by row-level security

Status: Accepted · Owner: Modelling agent · Blueprint `fc71a1458dce`

## Context

Salesforce sharing (role hierarchy, sharing rules, teams, territories) is org-wide; rebuilding it per module would drift.

## Decision

A shared access schema holds groups, the role hierarchy, teams, territories and share tables; every domain’s row-level security policies call the same functions; profiles and permission sets become Entra app roles and database roles.

## Consequences

Users see the same records in every module, through every client of the data; new domains inherit the model.

## Applies to (2)

- `access schema`
- `row-level security`
adrs.ADR-020:
# ADR-020: Build on open standards so the platform is portable

Status: Accepted · Owner: Modelling agent · Blueprint `fc71a1458dce`

## Context

The client wants to avoid trading one vendor lock-in for another.

## Decision

PostgreSQL for data, OCI containers for compute, OpenAPI 3 for APIs, CloudEvents for events, OpenID Connect and OAuth 2.0 for identity; only infrastructure templates and managed-service wiring are Azure-specific.

## Consequences

The platform can move to another cloud by rewriting infrastructure templates, not the application.

## Applies to (4)

- `PostgreSQL`
- `containers`
- `OpenAPI`
- `CloudEvents`
